Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

BLASTr (development version)

Breaking changes

  • The term “ASV” was dropped from the package API and documentation, since it denotes a sequence type specific to some pipelines. Sequences are now referred to only as seqs.
  • parallel_blast_old() lost its asvs argument; use query_seqs. This also fixes parallel_blast_old(), which still called get_blast_results() with the removed asv argument.
  • Example data inst/extdata/asvs_test.txt was renamed to seqs_test.txt.
  • parallel_blast() was rewritten. Instead of one blastn per sequence, the sequences are grouped in batches and each blastn searches a whole batch, so the database is read once per batch (in the benchmark on core_nt, 100 sequences took 79 s instead of 944 s, with the same hits):
    • total_cores is now the total number of threads to use. The number of processes, threads per process, batch size and mt_mode are chosen automatically from total_cores, the new ram_gb, the size of the database(s) and the number of sequences (see the new blast_strategy()). num_threads, batch_size and mt_mode (now NULL by default) only override the automatic choice.
    • num_alignments now defaults to 10 (was 4). With few alignments, BLAST cuts the hit list before the perc_qcov_hsp filter and valid hits can be lost.
    • Hit column k_indentity was renamed to k_identity (typo).
    • Subjects are reported by accession (saccver), as before.
  • parallel_blast() returns the long format by default: one row per hit, ranked by BLASTr (rank, tie, at_best, blast_rank), and one row with NA hit fields for each sequence without hits. The wide format (one row per sequence, hits 1_ to n_) is still available with output = "wide"; its k_ hits now follow BLASTr’s rank (BLAST’s order is in k_blast_rank). The summary per sequence (Check ID, …) comes from the new blast_summary().
  • Hits are ranked by rank_by (default "similarity", the Similarity score; or "identity", "bitscore"), no longer by BLAST’s order, which favours long alignments. check_tolerance is in the units of rank_by. The default was calibrated on sequences of known taxonomy: Similarity score and identity picked the right taxon significantly more often than bitscore (scripts in dev/benchmark/R/10_* to 12_*).
  • perc_qcov_hsp (80) no longer removes hits: BLAST searches with the new search_qcov_hsp (default 50) and the hits below perc_qcov_hsp are kept and flagged (low_qcov; summary Best low qcov). Removing them inside BLAST hid closer references that cover a bit less of the query (common with partial references) and promoted worse ones: in 66 ITS2 and rbcL sequences, 65 got a hit of another genus. With search_qcov_hsp = perc_qcov_hsp the search is as before.
  • Summary columns N hits at best identity and N taxids at best identity were renamed to N hits at best and N taxids at best (they follow rank_by).
  • get_tax_by_taxID() and get_tax_by_name() were rewritten: they ask the NCBI online through the E-utilities over HTTP (no Entrez Direct), in batches of 200 taxids and within the NCBI rate limit (optional API key), and return the same columns as get_tax(), for when the local taxonomy database is not there yet. get_tax_by_name() matches scientific names first, then synonyms and common names (matched_by). parallel_get_tax() is deprecated (use get_tax_by_taxID()).
  • install_dependencies() no longer installs Entrez Direct (efetch): nothing uses it now.
  • The internal, unexported search_primers_on_fq() was removed; the check of which primers are found in the reads is now detect_primers() in mtbrcdR.

New features

  • Reference databases: list_ncbi_blast_dbs() lists the BLAST databases of the NCBI with their sizes and dates; download_blast_db() downloads one (e.g. "core_nt"), checking the md5 of each file, into a directory named after its date, resumes interrupted downloads, and by default also gets taxdb and builds the taxonomy database of get_tax() for that date. make_unite_db() (UNITE general FASTA release, all eukaryotes or fungi) and make_silva_db() (SILVA SSU Ref NR99) download and format them as BLAST databases with NCBI taxids, so get_tax() and blast_lca() work as with the NCBI databases; UNITE names are matched to the NCBI taxonomy (the deepest name found; homonyms resolved by the higher ranks), SILVA gives the NCBI taxid of each record. A table next to the database records the taxid of each sequence and how it was found.

  • parallel_blast() results have a hit summary after Sequence: Check ID (“best ID” / “check ID”, agreement of the taxids of the best check_n hits, by default 10, comparing only hits within check_tolerance identity points of the best one), N hits, N taxids, N hits same taxid as 1st, N hits at best identity (1 = a single reference at the best identity) and N taxids at best identity (see check_hits()).

  • New k_Similarity score column for each hit, (10 * identity + qcovhsp) / 11 (formerly “BLASTn pseudo-score”; see similarity_score()).

  • Progress bar with the estimated time left (ETA), computed from the finished batches. In non-interactive sessions, one line per batch.

  • parallel_blast(background = TRUE) starts the search in a separate process and returns a job at once; blast_job_status(), blast_job_result(), blast_job_cancel() and blast_job_resume() follow it. The job lives in a directory (job_dir), so it survives the end of the R session and can be opened again with blast_job().

  • Several databases (a vector or a space-separated string in db_path) are searched together, smallest first; their sizes are added when choosing the strategy.

  • A sequence that makes BLAST fail is retried alone, so the others in its batch are not affected.

  • parallel_blast() searches search_alignments subjects (default 50) and keeps the num_alignments best ones that pass the identity and coverage filters: BLAST cuts its subject list before the coverage filter, so asking only for num_alignments could lose valid hits.

  • New task argument in parallel_blast() (BLAST -task, e.g. "dc-megablast").

  • New parallel_blast_hsps(): the raw hits in long format, one row per HSP, with the BLAST fields chosen in fields and no HSP limit or coverage filter unless asked. Searches a database or, with subject, the sequences of a FASTA file (BLAST -subject). Same batches, strategy, ETA, background jobs and log as parallel_blast().

  • All the hits tied with the best one (at_best) are kept, even beyond num_alignments. New summary columns Taxids at best (the tied taxids, for a lowest common ancestor) and At best truncated (the tie may go beyond the search_alignments subjects BLAST returned).

  • New hit fields nident and subject strand.

  • New as_blast_long(): converts wide results of any version (including k_indentity) to the long format, ranked with the same rules.

  • New get_tax(): taxonomy of taxids from a local SQLite database (NCBI taxdump, taxonomizr layout), in a fraction of a second for thousands of taxids. Takes taxids or any BLASTr result and returns one row per taxid: ranks, lineage, lineage_taxids and merged_into (merged taxids). When the database does not exist, it is built from the NCBI taxdump matching the date of the BLAST database of the search (or the one given), once, and kept in the BLASTr cache. make_taxonomy_db() builds it explicitly.

  • Uninformative references: parallel_blast() gains uninformative, the table of uninformative_references() (shipped in inst/extdata/uninformative_references.tsv: uncultured, metagenomes and MAGs, environmental samples, synthetic constructs and vectors, unidentified, chimeras, and wrong references by accession). The hits are flagged (informative, uninformative_category) and ranked among the informative ones, so rank, at_best, Check ID and blast_lca() use only those; a sequence with only uninformative hits keeps its best ones. blast_summary() gains N uninformative and Best uninformative score (a sign of a taxon missing from the database). The md5 of the table goes to the metadata and to the log; as_blast_long(uninformative = ) flags older results.

  • blast_lca() gains named_first: hits named only above genus (“Bacterium”, “Entolomataceae sp.”) do not vote when a named species is tied with them; and a species in open nomenclature (“Picea sp. X”) is ranked at its genus in LCA ranked ....

  • New blast_lca(): consensus lowest common ancestor of the hits tied with the best one (by default the deepest taxon holding 90% of them, so a few mislabelled references do not push the identification up), from the exact lineages of get_tax(). When the ancestor has none of the ranks of get_tax() (a clade, a superfamily), LCA ranked taxid/name/rank give the deepest ranked node above it, for tables by rank.

  • The BLAST command of each search (without the sequences) is kept in BLASTr_metadata$blast_cmd, with the BLAST version and the date of each database; it is shown in interactive sessions and written to the log.

  • Optional log of the searches: with log_dir (or the option BLASTr.log_dir / the environment variable BLASTR_LOG_DIR), each search adds a line to BLASTr_logs/blastr_runs.tsv with the number and lengths of the sequences, database size, strategy, time, CPU time and percentage of identifications. See blast_log_path() and read_blast_log().

Fixed

  • parse_fasta() failed on R 4.3 (could not find function "declare"): it called declare(), which only exists from R 4.4, to keep the carrier import. carrier was not used otherwise and left Imports.
  • blast_summary(): N hits, N taxids, N uninformative, N hits same taxid as 1st and Best uninformative score were computed only on the rows kept in the long results (the first num_alignments and the hits at best), not on all the subjects BLAST returned, as documented. parallel_blast() now computes them on all the subjects and keeps them in BLASTr_metadata$hit_counts, which blast_summary() uses; N hits equal to search_alignments now shows that BLAST returned a full list. The summary of the wide results and of the log is also computed on all the subjects. Results of older versions keep the old counts.
  • get_tax() ignored the Taxids at best column of wide results (it looked for its old name, Taxids at best identity, still accepted).
  • parse_fasta() names the missing file in its error message.
  • make_blast_db() accepts a taxid_map with any name (it required the base name of the FASTA file), checks that it exists, and prints the makeblastdb command only when verbose is not "silent".
  • The documentation of search_alignments in parallel_blast() named -max_target_seqs; the option passed to BLAST is -num_alignments.

Changed

  • parallel_blast(): search_alignments now defaults to 100 (was 50). In 1260 GenBank references searched in core_nt, it halved the sequences whose ties with the best hit were cut at the limit (170 to 94) and those whose ancestor differs from a search with 500 subjects (37 to 18), for 3% to 18% more time.
  • BLAST+ 2.17.0 (was 2.16.0), installed by install_dependencies() from bioconda in the conda environment blastr-blast-env; an environment created by an older BLASTr is recreated. On 300 GenBank references searched in core_nt, 2.17.0 gave the same hits, summary and ancestors as 2.16.0, in about the same time.
  • Which BLAST+ is used: the one of the conda environment; without it, the one of the system, only if it is 2.16.0 or newer (BLAST+ 2.12, for example, does not accept -mt_mode 2, used on large databases); otherwise an error that says to run install_dependencies(). Searches no longer install or update BLAST+. The source is kept in BLASTr_metadata$blast_source ("conda" or "system").
  • New has_blast(): whether BLAST+ 2.16.0 or newer is ready (conda environment or system), without installing anything. The examples and the vignette run their BLAST code only when it is TRUE.
  • Tests: the ones that run BLAST+ use the BLAST+ already installed and are skipped without it (before, they were skipped on CRAN, and the test setup created a new conda environment at each run). A real BLAST+ output (inst/extdata/blast_output_example.tsv, made by data-raw/blast_output_example.R) tests reading, ranking and summary where BLAST+ is not installed.
  • get_tax() no longer downloads the NCBI taxdump on its own: without the taxonomy database it stops and says how to get it, or asks in an interactive session. The new argument download = TRUE downloads the taxdump (about 80 MB) and builds the database, for those who use only get_tax(); download_blast_db() (taxonomy = TRUE), make_unite_db() and make_silva_db() still bring it with the BLAST databases.
  • New has_taxonomy_db(): whether get_tax() has its taxonomy database, without downloading or building anything; with db_path, the database of the date of the BLAST database(s) to be searched. A pipeline can check it at the start instead of stopping after the BLAST search.

Documentation

  • Examples that run in 22 of the 25 help pages of exported functions (5 before), with the small database in inst/extdata and a small taxonomy written in the example; they run only where blastn is found and write only to tempdir(). Titles, families of functions and the package page (?BLASTr) were rewritten.
  • New vignette “Get started with BLASTr” (vignette("BLASTr")); the vignette on searches in the background is now vignette("background-searches").
  • DESCRIPTION: SystemRequirements (BLAST+, Quarto) and biocViews.

BLASTr 0.1.7

Release Date: 2025-11-04

Development Changelog: dev

Added

  • New retry_times argument in parallel_blast() to specify the number of retries for failed BLAST jobs. Defaults to 10 times.

  • New verbose = "progress" in parallel_blast() to show a progress bar for the BLAST jobs.

  • New get_blastr_cache() for printing the directory used as cache for BLASTr.

  • The previous version of parallel_blast() is now available as parallel_blast_old(). It is kept for backward compatibility, but users are encouraged to switch to the new parallel_blast() implementation.

  • New exit_codes function to extract exit codes and error message from internal BLAST runs.

Changed

  • parallel_blast() will not throw errors immediately when a BLAST job fails. Instead, it will log the error and continue with the remaining jobs.

  • parallel_blast() output has a new attributes data frame with columns:

    • query_seq: The query sequence that was processed.
    • exit_code: The exit code of the BLAST command.
    • stderr: The standard error output from the BLAST command.

  • parallel_blast() will automatically retry failed BLAST jobs up to 3 times (or the value of retry_times) before giving up.

  • Argument asvs is renamed to query_seqs in parallel_blast().

  • Arguments asvs, out_file and out_RDS in parallel_blast() are now deprecated.

BLASTr 0.1.6

Release Date: 2025-10-28

Development Changelog: 0.1.6

Fixed

  • Fix hard coded num_threads = 1L in parallel_blast(). parallel_blast() now correctly uses the user provided num_threads argument.

  • Fix parallel functions not using the the custom compute profile. purrr::map do not have an argument for specifying the mirai .compute argument correctly. Now all parallel functions use the “default” mirai compute profile .compute = NULL.

  • Fix get_tax_by_taxID() when multiple tax IDs are provided.

  • Fix parse_fasta() concatenate lines for multiline FASTA.

BLASTr 0.1.5

Release Date: 2025-08-27

Development Changelog: 0.1.5

Added

  • New parallel framework based on native purrr functions, using mirai and carrier in the background.

  • New make_blast_db() function to create custom BLAST databases.

Changed

  • Internal entrez-direct version bump to 24.0.

  • The internal environments used by BLASTr have been renamed to blastr-blast-env and blastr-entrez-env.

  • Remove of the furrr based functions in favor of the new purrr native parallel.

  • All options() based parameters have been removed in favor of explicit arguments in the functions.

BLASTr 0.1.4

Changed

  • All functions have better defaults and less mandatory arguments.

Fixed

  • Fix progress bars when parallel processing is used.

BLASTr 0.1.3

Added

  • Refactor handling of internal errors.

  • shell_exec is not available anymore.

BLASTr 0.1.2

Added

  • New install_dependencies() automatically create environments.

  • Initial support for condathis for managing dependency installation.
